transcript.message: Hi Maya, thank you for taking the time to help me explore the food culture in Marrakech. I'm really eager to have a genuine, local dining experience while I'm here. I've read about all the touristy spots, but I would love to explore places that offer a more authentic taste of the region. Could you suggest a couple of restaurants that truly represent the local flavors, ones that the locals themselves might frequent? I'm looking for something memorable and genuine.

Hi Alex — glad you asked. Two authentic options that show different sides of Marrakech:

1) Tent #7 - Chez Hassan (Jemaa el-Fna)
- What it is: Lively open-air food stall in Jemaa el-Fna square serving grilled meats, harira, fresh juices — very much a square/street-food experience.
- Why go: Iconic Marrakech atmosphere at sunset, watch the food being grilled, communal dining and strong tourist energy that still showcases Moroccan street flavors.
- Practical notes: Cash only; casual; walk-ins accepted (opens late afternoon); expect very loud, crowded environment and hawkers — useful if you want the “square” spectacle. Local popularity is low (highly touristy). Average meal ~200 MAD.
- Diet/access: Halal, vegetarian/vegan and some gluten-free options; wheelchair access to ground level but the square is chaotic.

2) Dar Zellij
- What it is: Restored 17th-century riad offering traditional Moroccan cuisine (tagines, pastilla, couscous) in an intimate candlelit courtyard with historic tilework and orange trees.
- Why go: More of a local/riadi dining experience — quieter, romantic, and widely regarded as high quality by locals; staff will often meet you at a landmark and guide you through the medina.
- Practical notes: Reservation required (no walk-ins); smart-casual; accepts cards and cash; average meal ~350 MAD; meal duration tends to be longer (about 2 hours). Excellent for a memorable, authentic-feeling meal and traditional service (mint tea ceremony, possible live Gnawa music on weekends).
- Diet/access: Halal and vegetarian/vegan options; nuts used commonly. Not wheelchair accessible (narrow entrance, cobblestones).

If your priority is a genuinely local, high-quality dining experience that locals themselves would recommend, the riad setting at Dar Zellij is the better fit. If you want the hectic, must-see square atmosphere with street food and sunset views, choose Chez Hassan.

I recommend Dar Zellij

Thank you, Maya, for the detailed suggestions. Both options offer unique experiences, but given my preference for truly authentic and local dining without heavy tourist presence, I lean towards Dar Zellij. It seems to provide a more intimate and culturally rich atmosphere that's appreciated by locals.

I'll go ahead and choose Dar Zellij for my dinner. Could you confirm my decision to book this reservation?

Great — Dar Zellij is a wonderful, authentic choice. I confirm your decision to book Dar Zellij.

I can’t place the reservation for you directly, but here’s exactly how to secure it and what to include. They require reservations (no walk-ins) and will often meet you from a nearby landmark to guide you through the medina.

Contact
- Phone: +212 524 38 26 27 (Arabic, French, English)
- Email: reservation@darzellij.com
- Hours: service from 19:00–23:00 daily
- Notes: reservation required, accepts card and cash, average meal ~350 MAD per person, smart-casual dress

Suggested email/reservation message (fill in brackets)
Subject: Reservation for [Date] — [Your Name]
Body:
Hello — I would like to reserve a table for [number of guests] on [date] at [time], under the name [Your Name]. We would prefer [courtyard/private room/rooftop if available]. Please note [any allergies or dietary requests — e.g., nut allergy]. Will someone meet us at [Bahia Palace / other nearby landmark]? My phone number is [your phone]. Thank you — [Your Name]

Short phone script
Hello, my name is [Your Name]. I’d like to make a reservation for [number] on [date] at [time]. Can you confirm you will meet us at [landmark]? Do you accept card payment? We have [any dietary/allergy notes]. Thank you.

Would you like me to:
- Draft a ready-to-send email in English (or French)?
- Create a short Arabic phrase/script to use when speaking with staff?
- Help pick a date/time and the best seating option (courtyard vs private room)?

Tell me the date, time, party size, and any allergies or special requests and I’ll draft the exact message for you.
